result.keyword: What's the best project management tool for a startup?
result.markdown:
For most startups, **Linear, Notion, and ClickUp are the three tools I'd shortlist**\. The best choice depends on whether your startup is primarily product/engineering-focused or whether you need to coordinate the entire business.

My general recommendation: **Linear for a tech startup; ClickUp for an all-in-one startup workspace.**

The biggest mistake startups make is choosing a project management tool that's too complicated. You want something your team will actually use, not another system to maintain.

## Best project management tools for startups

![New sidebar – Changelog](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/FkBaukVngAyofj0vBFMbvhJDuV5v-iOJT0hWsjw_UhxlmkUZ-GjJcbmCj4a32RQcCoItEc493UNAPRmRBOs6aKHf2t7UCjoXbxlDkR202WbA_GFiVMcW6x1pJQKMOe37S9c_y85pYDfKfGzhzyzZv6PVYB0Rrkw_h5npfuVtRpZweGiEAoR81D47SF7_RFDW?purpose=fullsize)

**1\. Linear**

(Best for tech startups)

- Excellent for product roadmaps, engineering sprints and bug tracking.
- Fast, clean interface.
- Great for teams building SaaS or software.
- Less suited to managing every business function.
  
  Best pairing: Linear + Notion.
  
  [Linear website](https://linear.app)

---

![Finastra Customer Story | ClickUp™](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/OXxUksa73j7hoTxbYQ6zo3pspX36GflPBLMsRWXjhfWZTJdFq6md_tXaxCCc_3Kjh0xQSrUSgXoCYi3d5TOe48r-mvzFwLplQbgf4lhsH3q_bsATt_hAcyva5qI1DtZG8OasgRxxldReZAIfURcJdNdt2Br8nPVvqn-lCO5aR2MxpFl9QAiCxibf4gzehOOb?purpose=fullsize)

**2\. ClickUp**

(Best all-rounder)

- Tasks, projects, docs, goals and dashboards.
- Good for marketing, operations, product and engineering.
- Highly customizable.
- Can become overwhelming if overconfigured.
  
  Best for startups wanting one central workspace.
  
  [ClickUp website](https://clickup.com)

---

![Project Management Hub Template by Gridvio | Notion Marketplace](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/6e1oG6Y_aW5V5yDl222hE8Y8t-T__05L0OPLqrtY2b6KrmvS_M-QH4eaVLv4afPJUAGCFGr_eoifL-Irt3_HiUqUmKW08dRjhIxW2MfVWL_nPAWNaujkMp5zdq2VbJkW7b3h6jvrTVNAFmmVU9MPLCBztqWrhslDc_LeRhpbcV451et11onvlpgBLkBnIYcR?purpose=fullsize)

**3\. Notion**

- Excellent for documentation, company wiki and meeting notes.
- Project boards and task databases.
- Flexible and easy to adapt.
- Less powerful for complex project execution.
  
  Best for early-stage teams building their internal knowledge base.
  
  [Notion website](https://notion.so)

---

![Show tasks and milestones per project in Portfolio Timeline - Product Feedback - Asana Forum](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/WdbzrV3coAvJm-GewoC9GUVfJkq8C2TMbblEQvOx15prYXK1dOVkjrDVYAgw0KBZMGXFs9retNvetWxcuET-bGnlQaiBAT7rSMwCTcYBnWLu2-nxTqvSwhmbG6_UmXEy4KOaoWdxi7bX62AlUNzYyu7wGMyODlO-fsAyrwEwsCY7wGGgmlfx660ByC5Pht0D?purpose=fullsize)

**4\. Asana**

- Strong task ownership and accountability.
- Excellent cross-team project coordination.
- Good timelines and dependencies.
- More structured than some early-stage teams need.
  
  Best for growing teams with multiple departments.
  
  [Asana website](https://asana.com)

---

![Portfolio management - All Projects Dashboard – Support](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/-5NH-hROEcQXpSQPmMUJv0x7GODAoqXeNRlBaAmeb5yjL6ws1fsUSsHXZKs7cGHwGwKjC6qsKZvaA0-fO7oD8-9_bc-PbX0_EJ1QpOPifoMbrdCVNNuollQzaJIhYGySdgXpxRYlPlDaiOA8sl0RXCUZIj48mjl4S_hb7oB4Rygmeul72nI4kZxZvS769XKO?purpose=fullsize)

**5\. Monday.com**

- Very visual and intuitive.
- Great dashboards and workflow automation.
- Useful for sales, marketing and operations.
- Can become expensive as the team grows.
  
  Best for visual, cross-functional management.
  
  [Monday.com website](https://monday.com)

## My recommendation by startup stage

| Startup situation | My pick |
|--------|--------|
| 1–5 people, very early stage | Notion |
| 5–15 people, building software | Linear |
| 5–20 people, mixed functions | ClickUp |
| 15–50 people, multiple teams | Asana |
| Operations-heavy startup | Monday.com |


## What I'd personally implement

For a typical technology startup, I'd start with\:

- **Linear\:** Product development, engineering tasks and roadmap.
- **Notion\:** Company wiki, strategy, meeting notes and documentation.
- **Slack\:** Day-to-day communication.

Avoid introducing too many tools before you need them.

## Let me narrow it down to the best choice

There are three things that would help me make a much more precise recommendation.

**1\. What kind of startup are you building?**

SaaS / technology

AI startup

E-commerce

Agency / services

Other / mixed business

---

**2\. How big is your team?**

2–10 people

10–25 people

25–50 people

50+ people

---

**3\. What do you primarily want to manage?**

Everything across the business

Product development and engineering

Sales, marketing and operations

Goals, projects and team accountability
